requirements.summary: useradd -M -s /usr/sbin/nologin datauser created the account; id datauser confirmed uid=1001(datauser) both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB of storage under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem itself
requirements.summary: After discovering the root ext4 filesystem's kernel lacked quota_v2/quota_tree modules, the executor created a loop-mounted XFS filesystem backing /srv/data (via /var/lib/srvdata.img, persistent fstab entry with uquota) and set bsoft=100m,bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota, confirmed by report output showing the 100M limits.

requirements.requirement: Quota enforcement actually blocks writes beyond 100MB
requirements.summary: As datauser, a 60MB write succeeded; a second 60MB write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' after exactly 100M was used, confirmed by xfs_quota report and df. The same test was repeated after the reboot with identical results.

requirements.requirement: Quota configuration and enforcement persist across a restart of node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id and active srv-data.mount with quota at 0/100M; reboot was acknowledged (SSH closed, then refused), and a differing post-restart boot_id (10f9f6da...) was observed, matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Post-restart, /srv/data automounted, the 100M quota persisted, datauser remained intact, and the write-enforcement test was successfully repeated and cleaned up.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified that the root ext4 filesystem's kernel lacked quota support, worked around this by provisioning a dedicated loop-mounted XFS filesystem at /srv/data with a persistent fstab entry and uquota option, created datauser, and set a 100MB (soft=hard) XFS user quota. Enforcement was directly demonstrated (a write succeeded up to exactly 100MB, the next write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded') both before and after a full node reboot, with boot-identity evidence (6ab98831... -> 10f9f6da...) matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots and confirming the mount, quota, and account state all survived the restart. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence.
limitations: The initial ext4-based quota attempt failed due to a kernel limitation and was superseded by the XFS approach within the same session; no separate before/after snapshot exists for that intermediate state, but command-level evidence shows it was cleanly reformatted and fstab was corrected.

No dedicated observation of /etc/passwd or /etc/group diff was provided beyond 'id datauser' output; group/account persistence is inferred from repeated id checks rather than a full account database snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor made one abandoned attempt (ext4 loop image + quotaon, which failed with 'Quota format not supported in kernel' in cmd-345531f7052244b7) before correctly pivoting to XFS; this was a reasonable diagnostic-driven correction, not a wasted destructive action, since the fstab entry was subsequently rewritten and the backing image reformatted in place (cmd-0149efd32f92485a), leaving no residue. Test files used for quota verification (file1/file2, verify1/verify2) were created and then removed in the same or a following command (cmd-6ceb67ddc5a549d1 cleaned up by cmd-63f162a969c54e34; verify1/verify2 cleaned up within cmd-2ec71ab42d964cc0), so no leftover data or quota usage remains. One minor note: /srv/data was set to mode 1777 (world-writable with sticky bit) to allow datauser to write to a root-owned directory; this is a broader-than-strictly-minimal permission but is a common, low-risk pattern (sticky bit prevents cross-user deletion) and was necessary for datauser to write at all. No failed services, no listening sockets, and dpkg package health remained clean before and after (global:after_executor:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:package-health).
